plants.name: Paeonia lactiflora
plants.description: A long-lived herbaceous perennial with large, often fragrant, bowl-shaped to fully double blooms atop sturdy stems with deeply lobed, glossy green foliage. A classic cottage garden favorite that thrives in cold-winter climates.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to early summer (May to June in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Native to China, Mongolia, and Siberia; widely cultivated in temperate gardens across North America, Europe, and Asia
plants.funFact: Peonies can live and bloom for more than 100 years, and ants are often seen on the buds feeding on nectar, though they are not needed for the flowers to open.

plants.name: Rosa gallica
plants.description: A compact, suckering deciduous shrub and one of the oldest cultivated roses, bearing richly fragrant, semi-double flowers with golden stamens. It is the ancestor of many old garden roses.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to early summer (May to June)
plants.location: Native to southern and central Europe and western Asia; cultivated in temperate gardens worldwide
plants.funFact: Its dried petals retain their fragrance exceptionally well, so the Apothecary's Rose (Rosa gallica 'Officinalis') was used in medieval medicine and perfumery.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: A spectacular tree with fern-like foliage that is covered in clusters of trumpet-shaped lavender-blue flowers, which carpet the ground when they fall. It prefers warm subtropical climates.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring in the Northern Hemisphere subtropics (May to June); October to November in the Southern Hemisphere
plants.location: Native to South America (Argentina, Bolivia); cultivated in Mexico, the southern United States, the Mediterranean, South Africa, and Australia
plants.funFact: In Pretoria, South Africa, known as the Jacaranda City, there are tens of thousands of these trees, and in Mexico City they bloom in spring, turning streets purple.

plants.name: Digitalis purpurea
plants.description: A biennial or short-lived perennial that produces tall spikes of tubular, bell-shaped flowers with spotted throats, which are heavily visited by bumblebees. All parts of the plant are toxic.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to midsummer (May to July)
plants.location: Native to western and southwestern Europe and northwest Africa; naturalized in woodland clearings and roadsides in North America, Australia, and New Zealand
plants.funFact: Foxglove is the source of digoxin, a heart medication still in use today, derived from compounds first described medically by William Withering in 1785.
